name: Baking soda deodorant
summary: A DIY and natural-deodorant staple made with sodium bicarbonate; long used, but untested in trials.
lead: Baking soda deodorant refers to deodorants made with sodium bicarbonate, either commercial products or home-made mixtures applied to the underarms. Wikipedia lists sodium bicarbonate among the earliest patented deodorant ingredients and notes it appears in some dry and wet deodorants, alone or combined with other ingredients.

name: Apple cider vinegar for odour
summary: A home remedy of wiping vinegar on skin to curb odour; untested for this use, with burn warnings.
lead: Applying apple cider vinegar to the skin, typically the underarms, to reduce body odour is a folk remedy. Apple cider vinegar is about 5% acetic acid in water, made by fermenting apple cider, and is promoted for many health purposes.
claims: Wiping vinegar on the underarms removes or prevents body odour

name: Chlorophyll internal deodorant
summary: Oral chlorophyll or chlorophyllin pitched as an internal deodorant; the cited human evidence for body odor is essentially absent.
lead: Chlorophyll internal deodorant refers to the oral use of chlorophyll or its water-soluble semi-synthetic derivatives, chlorophyllins, to reduce body, breath or waste odor. Chlorophyllins are salts made from chlorophyll, and the main food-additive forms are sodium chlorophyllins, listed as E140(ii) and E141(ii).

name: Zinc for body odor
summary: Oral zinc is sometimes claimed to cut body odor; the sources consulted give no support for this use.
lead: Zinc for body odor refers to the claim, circulated in supplement and appearance communities, that taking zinc orally reduces body odor. Zinc is an essential mineral; oral forms such as zinc gluconate and zinc acetate are used to treat or prevent zinc deficiency.

name: Probiotics for body odor
summary: Probiotics are floated for body odor via the gut-skin link; no human trials were found.
lead: Probiotics for body odor is the idea that taking probiotic microbes, or altering the gut microbiome, changes how a person smells. Reference sources note that the gut microbiome can affect body odor, citing a 2020 study on cutaneous bacteria in the gut microbiome as biomarkers of systemic malodor.

name: Fruit and veg smell diet
summary: Eating more fruit and vegetables is associated with more pleasant-smelling sweat in a study of men; effects are described as mild.
lead: The fruit and veg smell diet is the practice of eating more fruit and vegetables in the belief that it makes sweat smell more pleasant. Wikipedia reports a study of males in which higher fruit and vegetable intake was associated with more pleasant-smelling sweat, described as floral, fruity, sweet and medicinal in quality.

name: Cutting red meat for smell
summary: A controlled study in men reportedly rated sweat from a meat diet as less pleasant; evidence is small.
lead: Cutting red meat for smell is the practice of reducing red meat intake in the belief that it improves body odor. Grokipedia states that red meat intake has been shown to alter axillary odor, making it less attractive to others, and describes a controlled study in which male participants ate meat or non-meat diets for two weeks, with samples from the meat group rated less pleasant and more intense.

name: Cutting garlic and onion
summary: Garlic compounds are documented in breath and skin emissions; avoiding garlic and onion is a plausible odor lever, with limited direct trials.
lead: Cutting garlic and onion is the practice of avoiding these foods to reduce body and breath odor. Garlic breath arises mainly from volatile sulfur compounds, especially allyl methyl sulfide (AMS), formed as allicin breaks down; AMS is the longest-lasting and can persist for up to two days.

name: Cutting alcohol for smell
summary: Dropping alcohol to smell better: a common anecdote with no dedicated studies behind it.
lead: Cutting alcohol for smell is a lifestyle practice in which people reduce or stop drinking alcohol in the belief that it will make their sweat, breath or general body odour less noticeable. It is discussed in appearance and grooming circles as part of a wider approach to smelling clean.
claims: Drinking alcohol makes sweat smell worse, so quitting improves body odour.

name: Carnivore diet smell
summary: Claims that eating only meat changes how you smell; reports go both ways and no one has measured it.
lead: Carnivore diet smell refers to claims about how an all-animal-product diet affects body odour, breath and sweat. Some adherents say their odour becomes milder, while others report the opposite.
claims: Eating only meat makes body odour neutral or less noticeable.
Carnivore eating can cause a stronger or fishy smell.

name: Fish odor syndrome choline restriction
summary: A diet approach to a rare genetic condition that makes sweat and breath smell fishy; managed by medical supervision.
lead: Trimethylaminuria (TMAU), also called fish odor syndrome, is a rare metabolic condition in which the body cannot adequately convert trimethylamine, a compound that smells like rotting fish, into odourless trimethylamine N-oxide. Choline restriction is one dietary approach discussed for managing it.

name: Washing clothes properly
summary: Basic laundry technique, raised in looksmaxxing mainly to stop clothes holding smell.
lead: Washing clothes properly is a grooming practice concerned with cleaning garments so that odour, dirt and stains are removed and fabrics last. In appearance communities it is raised mainly in connection with clothing that retains smell.

name: Laundry sanitiser and strip washing
summary: Extra washing tricks for smelly gym kit; popular anecdotes, no dedicated studies.
lead: Laundry sanitiser and strip washing are practices discussed for removing persistent odour from gym and sports clothing. Sanitisers are additives intended to kill microorganisms in the wash, while strip washing is a heavy soak and wash intended to remove built-up residue.
claims: Sanitiser or strip washing removes odour that normal washing leaves.

name: Wool and merino clothes
summary: Fine sheep wool said to resist odour; the claim is popular but untested in the sources reviewed.
lead: Merino is a fine, soft wool from the Merino sheep breed, used in clothing. In appearance and grooming discussions it is mentioned as a fabric that resists odour.
claims: Merino wool resists odour better than synthetics.

name: Cedar shoe inserts
summary: Wooden shoe trees said to soak up moisture and smell; popular in shoe care, with no trials on odour.
lead: Cedar shoe inserts are wooden pieces, often shaped like shoe trees, placed in footwear between wearings. A shoe tree is described generally as a device placed in a shoe to preserve its shape. In appearance and grooming communities they are discussed as a way to limit foot and shoe odour, since cedar is commonly said to absorb moisture and carry its own scent.
claims: Cedar absorbs moisture and odour from shoes

name: Foot powder
summary: Dusting powder for sweaty feet; sensible and cheap, but evidence is indirect.
lead: Foot powder is a dusting powder applied to the feet and sometimes inside shoes to absorb moisture and reduce odour, and some formulations contain antifungal or deodorant agents. It is used in grooming routines to manage foot sweat and odour.
claims: Foot powder keeps feet dry and cuts odour

name: Showering twice daily
summary: Morning and evening showers for odour control; common habit, no studies on the twice-daily part.
lead: Showering twice daily is a hygiene routine, usually morning and evening or after exercise, adopted in appearance-focused communities to control body odour and keep skin and hair clean. Personal hygiene is generally described as cleanliness practices for health and social acceptance, and norms vary by culture and era.
claims: Showering twice a day improves smell and skin presentation

name: Scent layering (body wash, lotion, fragrance)
summary: Stacking matched wash, lotion and fragrance to make a scent last; popular, untested.
lead: Scent layering is the practice of using matching or complementary scented products, such as body wash, lotion and fragrance, in sequence so the smell builds and lasts longer. The fragrance industry promotes a version of it: scented bath oil, shower gel or lotion in the morning, a lighter eau de toilette in the afternoon, and perfume at pulse points in the evening.
claims: Matching body wash, lotion and fragrance makes scent last longer

name: Fragrance signature scent
summary: Wearing one consistent fragrance so it becomes your identity; popular, untested.
lead: A signature scent is a single fragrance a person wears consistently so that others come to associate it with them. In appearance communities it is discussed as a memorability and personal-branding tool.
claims: A consistent signature scent makes you memorable

name: Hair perfume / hair mist
summary: Light fragrance spray for hair; a niche scent layer with no studies behind it.
lead: Hair perfume or hair mist is a light fragrance spray made for the hair, as an alternative to applying perfume to skin. It is used to leave scent in the hair and is discussed in grooming communities as a way to add a scent trail.
claims: Hair mist leaves a scent trail that lasts

name: Beard oil and balm scent
summary: Scented oils and balms for beards; mostly a grooming and fragrance choice with no clinical research behind the claims.
lead: Beard oil is a cosmetic product applied to the beard and the skin beneath it. It is made mainly from carrier oils and essential oils, and is intended to imitate the skin's natural sebum, keeping facial hair soft and manageable. Most products are scented, with fragrances ranging from sweet to bitter that are usually marketed as masculine, and they are sometimes used in place of cologne or aftershave.

name: Fragrance clones (dupes) / Zara
summary: Cheap lookalike perfumes, with Zara as the best-known retail example; popular for price, with no formal research on how they compare.
lead: Fragrance clones or "dupes" are inexpensive perfumes designed to smell like well-known designer or niche fragrances. Zara, the Spanish fast-fashion retailer owned by Inditex, sells perfumes and in 2021 launched a beauty line, ZARA Beauty. Online fragrance communities commonly discuss Zara and other budget brands as sources of scents resembling expensive designer releases.

name: Niche perfume / sample decants
summary: Small vials of perfume sold so people can test pricey scents first; a shopping practice, not an appearance intervention.
lead: Decants are small portions of a perfume transferred from a full bottle into a small vial, commonly sold so that buyers can test a fragrance before purchasing a full bottle. "Niche" perfumery refers to smaller houses whose products are positioned apart from mass-market designer releases and are often more expensive.

name: Sauvage / Bleu de Chanel compliment getters
summary: Two hugely popular men's designer scents that fragrance communities call crowd-pleasers; the compliment claims are anecdotal.
lead: "Compliment getter" is fragrance-community slang for a scent said to draw positive comments from other people. Dior Sauvage and Bleu de Chanel are two best-selling men's fragrances frequently named in this context.

name: Fragrance Reddit (r/fragrance) blind buys
summary: Buying fragrances unsmelled on community advice; a shopping habit with no research behind it.
lead: A "blind buy" is the purchase of a fragrance without first smelling it, often based on community reviews and recommendations. Online fragrance communities, including the r/fragrance subreddit, are described by members as a place to get such recommendations.

name: Oud and amber Middle Eastern fragrances
summary: Rich resinous and ambery scents rooted in Middle Eastern perfumery; much "oud" in stores is synthetic.
lead: Oud, or agarwood, is a resinous heartwood that forms in Aquilaria trees after infection by a mould; the tree produces resin as a defence and the wood darkens and becomes dense. It is a popular perfume ingredient, usually used as a base note and traditionally paired with rose. In the Arab world it is a long-standing aromatic burned as incense.

name: Attar oils / alcohol-free perfume
summary: Concentrated alcohol-free perfume oils with a long traditional history, discussed as a grooming scent option with no appearance research behind them.
lead: Attar (also spelled ittar) is a perfume oil made from botanical or other natural materials, usually by hydrodistillation or steam distillation, and sold in an oil base rather than in alcohol. It is worn as a fragrance, and in looksmaxxing and grooming discussions it appears as an alternative to alcohol-based colognes.

name: Vitamin C and zinc pit routine
summary: An anecdotal underarm-odor routine built on vitamin C and zinc, with no studies behind it.
lead: The "vitamin C and zinc pit routine" is an informal underarm-care practice discussed in grooming circles as a way to manage body odor, typically involving topical or dietary vitamin C and zinc. It is described as anecdotal, and no published studies of this specific routine were located.

name: Dermatologist referral for bromhidrosis
summary: Seeing a clinician to rule out medical causes of persistent body odor, such as hyperhidrosis or metabolic disorders.
lead: Bromhidrosis (osmidrosis) is foul-smelling body odor, often associated with excessive sweating that supports bacterial growth, especially in the underarms. In looksmaxxing discussions, getting a medical evaluation is raised as a way to check for an underlying cause of persistent odor.

name: Tea tree oil body wash
summary: A cleanser with tea tree oil used as a natural antibacterial wash; lab activity is shown but trials for odor or looks are absent.
lead: Tea tree oil body wash is a cleanser containing tea tree (melaleuca) oil, an essential oil distilled from Melaleuca alternifolia leaves. In grooming discussions it is used as a natural antibacterial wash, including for body odor and body acne.
